messages:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: P1 - KV prefix/prompt-cache amplification detected for hosted inference. Error rate up, token-serving latency spike. Paging eng-oncall and eng-sre.

ops-bot: Auto-mitigation attempted: scaled cache workers + autoscaling policy applied. Observed cache size still rising.

Ryan: on it. pinging in the bridge — starting quick triage. Can someone post impact numbers?

Maria: 95th latency for text-generation routes jumped from ~120ms to ~1.6s in last 3m. Cache entries grew 60x; evictions high but TTLs not pruning. Error 429 bursts to some customers — ~13 customers saw >50% error rates.

Devon: Adding logs:
```
kv_cache.size: 62_314_512
kv_cache.evictions_per_min: 12_048
continuous_batcher.batch_size: 256 -> observed 2048 under regen
tokenizer.hash_mismatch_count: 4_320
```

Sasha: Noted tokenizer drift on recent template rollout (took effect ~ 02:12 UTC). suspect hashing change + batching config allowed runaway keys.

Emily: Customer impact summary for CS: 13 customers with increased latency/errors; 3 on Dedicated saw tail-latency >5s for synth load tests; public API error rate up 7pp. No data exfil.

Ryan: Root cause hypothesis: recent prompt-template change + tokenizer model update changed prefix hashing -> cache miss churn -> continuous-batcher kept creating large batches/prefix keys -> KV cache amplification (hot keys with expanded tokenized length).

Maria: Repro steps locally: patch tokenizer -> generate same prompt list -> prefix keys length increased 3-4x -> creates new cache partitions.

Devon: Immediate mitigation plan (actionable):
- 1) Disable continuous batching for affected routes (quick config patch).
- 2) Hotfix tokenizer rollout -> revert to previous tokenizer hash function.
- 3) Limit per-request batch size to 128 and cap prefix key length (truncate to 256 bytes) as safety guard.
- 4) Kick TTL scrub job to aggressively evict suspect keys.

Sasha: Applying step 1 now: `curl -X POST https://ops-api.local/configs/batcher -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","continuous_batching":false}'` — returning 202. Deploying config to canary nodes.

ops-bot: Canary config applied to 6 nodes in us-west-2. Observing a 40% drop in batch_size within 90s.

Ryan: Rolling out step 3 (batch cap) globally via orchestration: `kubectl patch cm batcher-config -p '{"data":{"max_batch_size":"128"}}'` — patch applied.

Devon: Reverting tokenizer rollout (step 2) — creating rollback PR: `git revert -m 1 abc1234` -> pushing hotfix. CI -> green -> starting canary deploy of older tokenizer.

Emily: Noting customer comms draft: short note to affected customers, internal postmortem timeline to CS. No need for public status page yet but prepare one if errors persist.

ops-bot: TTL scrub triggered: `./scripts/kv_scrub --prefix-pattern 'prompt-*' --age-seconds 3600 --dry-run=false` — running now; rate-limited to avoid backend overload.

Maria: Early telemetry: error rate down 3pp after batcher disable on canaries; cache growth rate flattened. Latency improving on canaries to ~220ms.

Sasha: Tokenizer revert canary succeeded on 4 nodes; no regression in tests. Planning full roll after 10m observation.

Ryan: Escalation: if revert + batch cap doesn't stabilize within 15m, we will also throttle prefetch and disable KV prefill. Devon, be ready to flip prefetch flag.

Devon: On it. Command to flip prefetch: `opsctl feature-flag set kv_prefetch false --env prod` — queued, will execute only if needed.

eng-sre: Observability note — set temporary alert: if kv_cache.size rate-of-change > 10%/m trigger high, postmortem tag `prefetch-tokenizer-drift`.

ops-bot: Executed global batch cap patch, TTL scrub progress 45% after 4m.

Maria: After global cap, overall batch size distribution: p50=8, p95=64, p99=120. CPU usage on inference hosts down 28%.

Ryan: Good. Assigning roles for postmortem: Maria (telemetry), Devon (deploy/hotfix), Sasha (root cause writeup), Emily (customer comms), Ryan (incident lead). Handoff to next on-call in 50 minutes: @eng-oncall-next.

Emily: Drafting customer note: short, technical, actioned steps, ETA for full mitigation ~1h. Will link to internal postmortem.

Sasha: Root cause preliminary: tokenizer change introduced subtle whitespace normalization + different token IDs for some templates. Hashing function assumed canonicalized tokens; mismatch created new prefixes. Continuous-batcher groups by prefix-hash and unintentionally formed very large batches for a handful of hot templates, overloading KV store and preventing eviction from keeping up.

Devon: Post-mitigation checks: running canned evals across top 200 prompt templates — comparing tokenization output and prefix lengths. Script snippet:
```
for t in templates_top200.txt; do ./tokenize_old "$t" > /tmp/old && ./tokenize_new "$t" > /tmp/new; diff /tmp/old /tmp/new || echo "mismatch $t"; done
```
Found 11 templates with length change >30%.

Maria: Customer impact update: error bursts down to background levels for 9 of 13 customers. 4 customers still experiencing ~10-20% elevated errors — ops > investigating traffic skew.

Ryan: Next steps:
- Continue TTL scrub until key mass reduces to baseline.
- Full tokenizer revert complete across prod in 12m.
- Postmortem to include safer rollout flags, tokenization compatibility tests in CI, and a hard batch-size cap.

ops-bot: Tokenizer revert deployed to 100% of nodes at 1729000600. Monitoring.

Maria: After full revert and TTL scrub progress, p95 latency back to ~160ms, error-rate within normal variance. Cache size slowly trending down.

Emily: Customer note sent to impacted customers at 1729000720. CS triage queue opened for 4 customers needing direct follow-up.

Sasha: For permanent fix: 1) Add tokenization compatibility gate in CI comparing token IDs for canonical templates; 2) Make prefix-hash include tokenizer-version tag so mismatches cause separate cache namespace instead of collisions; 3) Add safety cap on batcher creating batches >512 and circuit-breaker to fall back to single-request mode.

Devon: Filed follow-ups: GH-981 (tokenizer-compat-tests), GH-982 (prefix-hash-versioning), GH-983 (batcher-circuit-breaker).

Ryan: Incident status: mitigated/monitoring. Handing off to eng-sre for watch. Will keep thread open for any regressions. Great rapid response. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident auto-close scheduled in 8h unless manually closed.

eng-sre: Taking watch. Will alert if any metric backslides.

end of thread: Ryan: closing personal on-call shift notes and linking to postmortem docs when ready.
